newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot naphtha drifts lower but swaps stable.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot naphtha drifts lower but swaps stable.

text.p: European naphtha prices drifted lower in line with weaker crude futures. Traders said lengthy supplies and slack end-user demand were also adding pressure.

Spot market prices drifted lower in line with crude and trade was further dulled by an Industry function but swaps were reported traded at a steady $174 and $174.50 a tonne cif NWE with the market showing a steady contango of $1.50 to $2.50 a tonne out to September.
Prompt lifting barges were notionally pegged around $2 lower at $167/$169 a tonne fob ARA with cargoes of $1-2 at $173/$175 cif NWE.

Traders reported sufficient end-user buying interest to balance fresh Russian cargo avails in the Mediterranean, but weaker crude and refiner selling left prices slightly softer at around $169/$173 a tonne cif Med.
